title: Exactness on each graded component
statement: Let R be a commutative ring with a decomposition R=\bigoplus_{n\in\mathbf Z}R_n into additive subgroups such that R_aR_b\subseteq R_{a+b} (a \mathbf Z-graded ring). A graded R-module is an R-module B with a decomposition B=\bigoplus_{n\in\mathbf Z}B_n into additive subgroups such that R_aB_b\subseteq B_{a+b}; an R-linear map u:A\to B of graded R-modules is degree-preserving if u(A_n)\subseteq B_n for every n. Let 0 \to A \to B \to C \to 0 be an exact sequence of graded R-modules with degree-preserving maps. For every n\in\mathbf Z, the sequence 0 \to A_n \to B_n \to C_n \to 0 of restricted maps is exact.

source.place: Algebra, Section 00JL (section-graded), the graded-module exactness convention

proof.text: Let i:A\to B and p:B\to C be the maps in the short exact sequence. If a\in A_n and i(a)=0, exactness of the original sequence gives a=0; since i preserves degrees, its restriction A_n\to B_n is therefore injective.

source.place: Algebra, Section 00JL (section-graded), the graded-module exactness convention

proof.text: Let b\in B_n satisfy p(b)=0. Exactness gives a\in A with i(a)=b. Write the finite homogeneous decomposition a=\sum_j a_j with a_j\in A_j. Degree preservation gives i(a_j)\in B_j, while b is homogeneous of degree n. Uniqueness of the direct-sum decomposition of B implies i(a_n)=b (and i(a_j)=0 for j\ne n), so every element of ker(B_n\to C_n) lies in the image of A_n\to B_n.

source.place: Algebra, Section 00JL (section-graded), the graded-module exactness convention

proof.text: For c\in C_n, surjectivity of p gives b\in B with p(b)=c. Write b=\sum_j b_j with b_j\in B_j. Since p preserves degrees, p(b_j)\in C_j, and since c is homogeneous of degree n, uniqueness of the direct-sum decomposition of C gives p(b_n)=c. Thus the restricted map B_n\to C_n is surjective, completing exactness of 0\to A_n\to B_n\to C_n\to0.
